title: How Retailers Can Plan for 2027 Minimum Wage Changes
summary: Sixteen states raise the minimum wage January 1. Ten meet or beat the 3.5% median merit increase budget. Here’s how retailers can plan pay for 2027.
body_markdown:
On January 1, 2027, sixteen states will increase their minimum wage. For retail leaders, now is the time to focus on identifying where and by how much[labor costs](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/cost-of-labor-vs-cost-of-living) will rise.


Twelve of the sixteen increases range from about 3% to 4%. Michigan, Virginia, and Rhode Island will see larger increases of 6% to 9%, while Nebraska's is below 2%. This variation means multi-state retailers should avoid using a single company-wide labor assumption.


## Minimum wage changes coming January 1


Michigan, Virginia, and Rhode Island have the largest increases, while Nebraska and California have the smallest. Fifteen rates are confirmed. Vermont's inflation-based rate will be announced in early January.


‍


New York's standard minimum wage will remain at $17.00 for NYC, Long Island, and Westchester, and $16.00 for the rest of the state in 2027. However, a proposal could[increase rates on March 1, 2027](https://www.governor.ny.gov/new-york-state-minimum-wage-2027) , so monitor developments closely.


## What minimum wage changes mean for your budget


The increase affects your lowest-paid roles, but its impact extends further. When entry-level wages rise, employees in roles just above—such as shift leads, keyholders, and experienced associates—may earn only slightly more than new hires. Most retailers address this by raising those rates as well, so the actual cost of a 4% minimum wage increase is usually higher than 4% of your minimum-wage payroll.


Two additional factors may affect teams. In some states, including California and Washington, the salary threshold for exempt roles is tied to the state minimum wage, which can increase pay for assistant and store managers. Also, if local regulations set a store's pay, a city or county minimum may already exceed the state rate, so the state increase may have less impact than expected.


## Where the increases outpace standard 2027 merit budgets


Ten of the sixteen increases are at or above 3.5%, the overall median merit budget U.S. companies plan for 2027, according to the[2027 Pave Compensation Budgets & Planning Report](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/merit-budgets-2027) with Alpine Rewards.


This means that the mandated minimum wage increases can have much broader talent implications. The[3.5% is a median budget](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/merit-budgets-2027) across payroll, not what everyone receives. In fact, 87% of surveyed companies use individual performance ratings to set merit increases, so a solid performer may receive less than the median.


‍


Two other findings from this survey are important for retailers. Promotions are a stronger lever, with average increases of 9% to 12%, about three times a typical merit raise. Promoting shift leads and keyholders is a direct way to restore the pay gap. Additionally, 80% of surveyed companies include salary ranges in every U.S. job posting, so candidates and employees will see the new entry-level rate.


## 4 budget planning tips for retailers


1. **Develop your labor budget by state rather than company-wide.** Apply each state's specific increase to the hours and headcount in its stores, and include the additional cost of maintaining pay ranges.
2. **Review pay compression before finalizing pay ranges.** Identify all roles within about one dollar of the new minimum wage. Determine which rates should be adjusted to maintain a meaningful gap between new hires and leads, and compare your merit guidelines for those roles with the floor increase in each state.
3. **Consider the increase in relation to hours, scheduling, and pricing.** If certain states face higher costs, decide early whether to adjust staffing, scheduling, or pricing, rather than waiting for Q1 results.
4. **Prepare logistics before the new year.** Update payroll systems and posted notices in each affected state, and inform managers and employees about upcoming changes to ensure the first January paycheck meets expectations.


## 3 things still to watch


Some figures are not final, so build flexibility into your planning:


- **Vermont:** The rate is inflation-based and will be announced in the first week of January; the table uses a projected rate of approximately $14.91.
- **New York:** The standard wage is frozen for 2027, but a proposal could raise it on March 1, 2027, to $17.60 for NYC, Long Island, and Westchester, and $16.55 for the rest of the state, pending legislative approval. Home care aides will receive an increase on January 1.
- **Local rates:** Many cities and counties set their own minimum wages and may change them on different dates. Review each store's local rate in addition to the state rate.


## The retail takeaway


Most increases are modest, but the most effective plan is built store by store. Set the appropriate rate for each state, account for the domino effect on higher roles, check your merit budget against the floor increase, and keep a list of items to review in January. Starting this process in November allows for careful decision-making.
